findings.title: Denial cache has no invalidation and can override fresh allows
findings.body: `Check` returns immediately from `permDenialCache` before consulting `permCache` or the DB, and `permDenialCache.Set` is called after any DB-backed denial. Nothing invalidates these entries when permissions are granted or when a new dashboard/folder is created. A denied check (for example, before a just-created dashboard's creator permission is visible, or before an admin grants a role) therefore keeps returning Allowed=false for the 30s shortCacheTTL even after the DB grants access. This also means a stale denial overrides a later-refreshed allow in permCache, which directly undermines the PR goal of making newly created resources accessible. Deny entries need invalidation, or must not override a fresh cached allow, and likely deserve a shorter TTL.

findings.title: Denial cache key uses raw subject ID and omits identity type
findings.body: The denial-cache key is built from the raw subject ID (`checkReq.UserUID`) before `GetUserIdentifiers` resolves the canonical UID, and it does not include the identity type. The permission cache, in contrast, is keyed by the resolved `userIdentifiers.UID`. The same user can therefore have separate denial entries for `user:123` and `user:<uid>`, so the denial cache is bypassed when the subject form changes. Conversely, identities such as `user:123`, `service-account:123`, or `anonymous:123` share the same denial key even though they can represent different principals; a denial for one can be served for another until TTL expiry. Resolve the subject first and include the identity type plus canonical UID, and escape or hash the key components.

findings.title: No test that Check populates the denial cache
findings.body: The new test for the denial cache only seeds `permDenialCache` manually; it does not exercise a normal denied `Check` and verify that the denial entry is written. A bug in the key used by `s.permDenialCache.Set` or a missed Set call would pass the current tests. Add a case with a denying fake permission store that asserts a second identical `Check` is served from the denial cache without incrementing `store.calls` and still returns Allowed=false.
